children: will spend as much as $8.5B to bring customers back to the Golden Arches by making big investments in menu innovations, modernizing its restaurants, and creating a more welcoming and efficient workforce.

, the company’s new initiative to drive operating margin to low- to mid-50% by 2030 and 250 basis points of restaurant-level efficiency gains, will be discussed at Wednesday’s investor day presentation as the hamburger chain goes all in on efforts to restore its position in the competitive fast food industry and prop up its declining share price.

The 250 basis point target of restaurant efficiency translates to ~$100K in annual cash flow benefits for the average U.S. restaurant, the majority of which is expected to benefit the restaurant’s bottom line over time. The company estimates these investments will generate an approximately four-year payback for franchisees.

“We are confident that executing across the key components of NEXT will unlock stronger restaurant economics, generate attractive returns for the company, our franchisees, and shareholders, and increase capacity to keep investing in growth,” said the company’s CEO, Chris Kempczinski.
The $8.5B price tag to modernize its restaurants, improve technology, and make its operations more efficient will be front-loaded with $5B to be spent through 2030 and the remainder through 2036.

The investments are expected to contribute nearly 2.5% to systemwide sales growth in 2027, moderating to around 2% by 2030; free cash flow conversion of mid-to-high 80% range by 2030; and general and administrative expenses comprising 1.9% of systemwide sales by 2030.
expects to gain 1.5 percentage points in chicken share and 1.5 percentage points in beverage share by 2030, as well as maintain beef-share leadership.
